provenance: M6 cold review, finding 2. `near-excludes-its-own-anchor` needed the anchor's own element out of the candidate set; the implementation excluded the anchor **and every ancestor of it**, which is a strictly larger rule that no case tested — in that case the anchor's ancestors are `tr`/`table`/`body`, so `c === anchor` would have satisfied it identically. The larger rule breaks the commonest use of proximity there is: the row, card or list item that CONTAINS the value. Worse than unreachable — the next sibling container wins on the forward tie-break, so 'which row costs $24.50' answered 'Cobalt Floor Rug $18.00': a different product at a different price, reported as success with a PASS verdict.

triage.what_this_grades: that containment ranks ahead of adjacency. A candidate wrapping the anchor is not near the anchor, it holds it, and that is nearer than any neighbour can be. Only the anchor's own element stays excluded — `near` means beside or around, never is.
triage.watched_red: before the fix: status success, answer 'Cobalt Floor Rug $18.00'.
triage.why_the_anchor_is_the_price: the entity this task names is the price, not the product — the product is what is being asked for. Anchoring on the answer would make the identity check unfalsifiable (verifier-anchor-not-self-satisfied), which is the flaw the same cold review found in tc1-shop-price-near.
